entries.content:
Parallel web search in fast mode is now free on AI Gateway through January 31, 2027, and Parallel is now the default web search for eve agents.

The tool works with any AI Gateway model, with no separate Parallel API key. Parallel finds relevant web pages and returns links with short excerpts. You can filter results by website or publication date.

In eve, the built-in 

web_search
tool uses Parallel fast mode automatically when the model is served through AI Gateway. See the eve documentation for other search configurations.

To use Parallel fast mode with the AI SDK, add 

gateway.tools.parallelSearch({ mode: 'fast' })
to your tools: 
      
import { gateway, generateText, stepCountIs } from 'ai';
const { text } = await generateText({  model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-terra',  prompt: 'What are the latest developments in AI this week?',  tools: {    parallel_search: gateway.tools.parallelSearch({ mode: 'fast' }),  },  stopWhen: stepCountIs(3),});

Search the web with Parallel fast mode using the AI SDK.

The offer covers fast mode only, with Zero Data Retention enabled by default. Other modes are billed at standard pricing.

Learn more in the web search documentation.

entries.title: Introducing Vercel X
entries.summary: Today we’re launching Vercel X, a six-week accelerator for AI founders at the idea and pre-seed stages.Join a cohort of 40 teams at our San Francisco HQ and build alongside Vercel’s product leaders, designers, and engineers.The program takes no equity for participation and offers access to a program-wide pool of more than $9M in credits from Vercel, AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other partners.Appli
entries.content:
Today we’re launching Vercel X, a six-week accelerator for AI founders at the idea and pre-seed stages.

Join a cohort of 40 teams at our San Francisco HQ and build alongside Vercel’s product leaders, designers, and engineers.

The program takes no equity for participation and offers access to a program-wide pool of more than $9M in credits from Vercel, AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other partners.

Applications are now open through November 29, 2026. The program runs from January 19 to March 2, 2027.

Vercel has worked with more than 100 early-stage teams from around the world across three accelerator cohorts. Alumni include Rex, Alloy Robotics, Interfaze, Cervo, and Hacktron. Interfaze and Rex are backed by Y Combinator, and Cervo was acquired by Altana Technologies.

You're building next to the best operators in the world who are pushing you to ship and move faster. Vercel gave us the clarity and conviction to scale, build credibility for YC, and then raise from VCs.Merlin KafkaCEO, Rex

Copy link to headingWhy Vercel X?

If you’re applying to Vercel X, you probably have an idea or project you haven’t been able to stop thinking about. The next stretch is figuring out exactly what you’re building and who it’s for.

We think you get through that stretch the Vercel way: by deeply understanding your customers, shipping quickly, and iterating to greatness.

The program includes:

  • Technical mentorship: Hands-on workshops and product feedback from Vercel’s design, product, and engineering teams.

  • Partner credits: Put credits toward hosting, compute, and model API usage as you build and test your product.

  • Founder community: A cohort of AI founders at the same stage, with weekly fireside chats featuring industry leaders.

  • Investor access: Mentorship from VC partners and the opportunity to present your company to investors, ecosystem partners, and the Vercel community at Demo Day.

Winning teams receive funding from Vercel Ventures and prizes from program partners.

Copy link to headingWho should apply

We’re looking for technical builders with ambitious ideas and insatiable curiosity.

You don’t need a finished product or traction. Tell us what you want to build, who needs it, what AI makes possible, and why you’re the right person or team for the job.

Solo founders and teams of up to three can apply from around the world. You must be a Vercel customer and must not have participated in a traditional VC accelerator or raised an institutional seed round. See the additional eligibility requirements below.

All participants must spend the full six weeks in San Francisco and attend weekly events in person.

Vercel X is for those who have the conviction to go against the grain and start building. I started building on the internet at ten, in Lanús, with a Windows 95 PC and no one telling me what was possible. Pushing for change doesn’t come by waiting for consensus. The next generation of software is being built now. We’re showing up for builders turned founders as their first supporters.Guillermo RauchCEO, Vercel

Copy link to headingApply to Vercel X

Applications close at 11:59 p.m. PT on Sunday, November 29, 2026. Decisions will be released in mid-December.

Applicants must be Vercel customers at or above the age of majority in their jurisdiction, able to commit to the full six weeks in person, and not located in or otherwise subject to restrictions imposed by U.S. sanctions laws.

Vercel X program applications will be judged on the quality of the submission, the founder's background, and the overall potential for impact.

Contributors

Logan Liffick, Skully Paoli, Luis Gutierrez Rico, Marijana Pavlinić

entries.title: Gemini 4 Neon now available on AI Gateway
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Neon from Google is now available on AI Gateway.Gemini 4 Neon is a major upgrade over the earlier, lighter Gemini 4 model, delivering output quality close to Google’s larger Gemini 4 models with faster responses. It’s built for coding, agent workflows, and multi-step tasks.The model accepts text, images, video, and documents, with a 1M-token context window. It supports tool calling, struc
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Neon from Google is now available on AI Gateway.

Gemini 4 Neon is a major upgrade over the earlier, lighter Gemini 4 model, delivering output quality close to Google’s larger Gemini 4 models with faster responses. It’s built for coding, agent workflows, and multi-step tasks.

The model accepts text, images, video, and documents, with a 1M-token context window. It supports tool calling, structured outputs, grounding with Google Search and Google Maps, and four reasoning levels: low, medium, high, and xhigh.

Use 

google/gemini-4-neon
as the model ID: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'google/gemini-4-neon',  prompt: 'Write a TypeScript function that debounces async calls.',});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use Gemini 4 Neon in Codex, Cursor, or another supported agent, see the coding agents guide.

Try Gemini 4 Neon in the model playground, or explore all language models.

A new read-ahead algorithm uses your application’s access patterns to load data from persistent storage before it’s needed, reducing the time your code spends waiting.All drives get this update automatically, with no SDK upgrade or configuration changes required. Read pricing is unchanged.Learn more in the Ver
entries.content:
Vercel Drives now reads files up to 6x faster.

The update improves cold-read performance. A new read-ahead algorithm uses your application’s access patterns to load data from persistent storage before it’s needed, reducing the time your code spends waiting.

All drives get this update automatically, with no SDK upgrade or configuration changes required. Read pricing is unchanged.

Learn more in the Vercel Drives documentation.

entries.content:
Instant deployments let you deploy eligible static sites to Vercel in about a second, without a build step. They now support CSS, images, fonts, and other assets alongside HTML and Markdown.

Deploy a landing page with its stylesheet and images, or a report created by your coding agent, through the Vercel CLI or REST API. With the CLI, run:

      
vercel deploy ./my-static-site  Inspect         https://vercel.com/acme/my-static-site/8smhGjsosANjMqstetZ2CBb35fbB  Preview         https://my-static-site-j7xexfrjw-acme.vercel.app✓ Ready in 1s

Deploying a static site in one second with the Vercel CLI.

Newly supported file types include:

  • Styles and data: CSS, JSON, XML, plain text, and web manifests

  • Images: SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, and ICO

  • Fonts: WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, OTF, and EOT

  • Documents and media: PDF, MP4, WebM, MP3, WAV, and OGG

Instant deployments support up to 100 files totaling 25 MB or less. Vercel detects eligible deployments automatically, with no configuration required.

Deployments that exceed these limits, include JavaScript or other unsupported files, or are triggered by Git still build as before. The same applies to projects with a framework preset, custom build settings, a root-level 

package.json
or Vercel configuration file such as 
vercel.json
, or a 
public/
directory.

This update is rolling out across all plans. Learn more in the deployment documentation.

entries.title: Vercel Blob now supports TTLs for automatic deletion
entries.summary: Vercel Blob can now delete blobs automatically. Pass ttlDays when you write a blob and it is deleted that many days after upload, from 1 to 730 days. The TTL counts from the blob's upload date.Use TTLs for blobs you would otherwise delete yourself, such as session transcripts, exports, and temporary uploads.ttlDays works on put(), copy(), putImage(), multipart uploads, and presigned upload URLs. E
entries.content:
Vercel Blob can now delete blobs automatically. Pass 

ttlDays
when you write a blob and it is deleted that many days after upload, from 1 to 730 days. The TTL counts from the blob's upload date.

Use TTLs for blobs you would otherwise delete yourself, such as session transcripts, exports, and temporary uploads.

ttlDays
works on 
put()
, 
copy()
, 
putImage()
, multipart uploads, and presigned upload URLs. Every write result and 
head()
response now includes 
expiresAt
, so you know when a blob is due for deletion. 
      
import { put, setTtl } from '@vercel/blob';
// Delete this export 7 days after uploadconst blob = await put('exports/report.csv', csv, {  access: 'private',  ttlDays: 7,});
console.log(blob.expiresAt); // 2026-11-24T00:00:00.000Z
// Change your mind later: extend to 30 days, or clear it with nullawait setTtl(blob.url, { ttlDays: 30 });await setTtl(blob.url, { ttlDays: null });

    

setTtl()
changes or removes the TTL of blobs you already have, one URL or up to 1,000 at a time, without re-uploading them.

In 

Vercel CLI 65.16.0
and later, pass 
--ttl-days
to 
vercel blob put
, 
put-image
, 
copy
or 
presign
, and use 
vercel blob set-ttl
on existing blobs. 
      
vercel blob put report.csv --ttl-days 7vercel blob set-ttl exports/a.csv exports/b.csv --ttl-days 30vercel blob set-ttl exports/a.csv --clear-ttl

Setting a TTL costs one Advanced Operation per started 60 days, on top of the write. A 7-day TTL costs one, and the 730-day maximum costs 13. Clearing a TTL and the deletions themselves are free. You can track TTL operations in the Blob section of the Observability tab.

npm install @vercel/blob@2.9.0

Learn more in the Vercel Blob documentation.

entries.summary: Speed Insights now measures soft navigations: client-side route changes that update page content without a full reload. This means you can now track performance as users move through your app, not just on full-page loads.Speed Insights captures LCP, FCP, INP, and CLS for soft navigations and includes these measurements in your Real Experience Score. TTFB is not captured because there is no new doc
entries.content:
Speed Insights now measures soft navigations: client-side route changes that update page content without a full reload. This means you can now track performance as users move through your app, not just on full-page loads.

Speed Insights captures LCP, FCP, INP, and CLS for soft navigations and includes these measurements in your Real Experience Score. TTFB is not captured because there is no new document request.

Soft-navigation tracking is enabled by default for all projects using Speed Insights, with no action required. It works with modern web frameworks such as Next.js, SvelteKit, and Nuxt, in Chromium-based browsers.

In your project's Speed Insights dashboard, use the new Navigation Type filter to view All, Hard, or Soft navigation data.

Soft-navigation events count toward Speed Insights Plus usage. For existing projects that had Plus enabled before this release, Speed Insights events from soft navigations will not be charged until December 1. For projects that newly enable Plus, these events are billed from the start.

To disable soft-navigation tracking, set 

softNavs
to 

false
in your application code and redeploy. This option requires 
@vercel/speed-insights
version 2.1.0 or later: 
      
// orinjectSpeedInsights({ softNavs: false });

Disable soft-navigation tracking in your application.

Learn more in the Speed Insights documentation.

entries.content:
A new Ignored Build Step preset lets you skip preview builds for branches without an open pull request. Production deployments and previews for branches with open pull requests continue to build.

On GitHub and GitLab projects, skipped preview deployments are canceled before consuming any Build CPU Minutes.

To enable this, open your project’s Deployments > Configuration. Under Ignored Build Step, select Only build previews for pull requests from the Behavior menu and click Save.

Learn more in the Ignored Build Step documentation.

entries.content:
Today we're announcing eve 1.0, the open-source framework for building production-ready agents.

Since the public preview in June, we've worked with early adopters to prepare eve for 1.0, shipping 230+ releases and merging thousands of pull requests. With this release, eve is now generally available.

We've made eve faster, expanded integrations, and improved observability. Security controls let you decide which actions need approval and what data gets collected. We've also made it easier for coding agents to build with, measuring that experience with a rigorous evaluation suite.

With eve handling your harness and infrastructure, you and your agent can focus on building instead.

Copy link to headingBuild production agents on a harness you own

The harness in eve is the loop that calls models, runs tools, and delegates work to subagents. You choose the model, add or replace tools, edit instructions, and decide which actions need approval. The open-source Workflow SDK saves progress as the agent runs, so it can pick up from its last completed step after a crash. Multiplayer sessions and agent-to-agent calls are built in.

For managed hosting, deploy your eve agent to Vercel. Vercel Workflows handles durable execution, and Vercel Sandbox runs agent-generated code in isolation.

Build software factories that turn requests into tested pull requests, company brains that answer questions from your business data, or customer-facing agents in your product.

Thousands of businesses already run eve in production for internal and customer-facing agents. Rillet built a software factory on eve that takes in customer requests, converts them into specs, tests the changes, and opens PRs for human review. Rillet tripled its shipping rate in three months. Clay built monty, a data agent that answers employees’ questions in Slack. Just over two months in, 30–40% of the company used it every week.

Lindy's agent framework roundup names eve “Best for durable backend agents”.

Custom agents built with eve plus Vercel workflows. I’m biased but I didn’t mandate this, we felt it was the best solution for us.Mitchell Hashimoto(opens in new tab)

Copy link to headingCollaborate in multiplayer agent sessions

Multiplayer lets several people work with an agent in one shared session. eve keeps track of who said what and directs approvals and sign-ins to the right person. You can set up memory for each user or the whole team.

In the native Slack channel, each thread is one shared session. Approvals appear as buttons that only the right person can answer, and a live task card shows progress and timing. You can follow up in the thread without mentioning the agent again, cancel the current turn, or reset the session from Slack.

Ambient mode lets an agent listen in channels you choose, even without being mentioned. Guided by goals you set per channel, it decides when to speak up, help, or take on a task, and when to stay quiet. To limit model costs, a small decision model screens every message first, and only the ones that might be for the agent start a turn.

Slack is one of several native channels, alongside Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, GitHub, Linear, Twilio, Web Chat, and iMessage. The Chat SDK channel adds support for any Chat SDK platform adapter, including WhatsApp, Messenger, Google Chat, and email. Each channel is one file, and the same agent can work across all of them. See the integrations directory for the full list.

Copy link to headingBuild agent UIs with Next.js and other frameworks

eve 1.0 expands our native integrations for Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, and Vite. The framework integrations build your agent alongside your app and set up its routes. On Vercel, you can deploy the agent and your site as one project, or host them separately.

The client libraries let you work with tool calls, approval requests, and questions in a consistent way across frameworks. Use that session data to build custom UIs: stream replies into agent chats, embed an agent in a page, or show the agent's tool calls in your own components.

Use 

eve add channel/web
to scaffold a chat app with AI Elements components, or add eve's React, Vue, or Svelte bindings to an existing UI.

Copy link to headingBuild multi-tenant agents

One support-agent deployment can connect to each customer's ticketing system with their own credentials and apply that customer's approval rules.

Your application authenticates the user and identifies which tenant they belong to. You can then set memory, connection credentials, and approval policy for that tenant and user.

Before each model call in the main agent loop, dynamic definitions load the agent's capabilities from the session and external data. In 1.0, they cover models, connections, and subagents as well as tools, skills, and instructions.

Copy link to headingGive agents memory across sessions

We added native memory so agents can carry context from one session to the next. You choose the memory's scope and can use the built-in file memory, a memory provider, or one you build yourself.

Built-in 

fileMemory
keeps data in memory in 
eve dev
and in a private Vercel Blob store you configure on Vercel.

Other providers include claude-mem, Hindsight, Kybernesis Arcana, Memanto, memco, Supermemory, and Upstash AgentKit.

Copy link to headingTrace agents with OpenTelemetry

We rebuilt eve’s tracing around OpenTelemetry, so you can follow an agent’s work in the tracing tools you already use. 

eve dev
records traces locally by default. If you host eve yourself, you can export them to an OpenTelemetry backend, including one you run yourself.

Tracing integrations include Raindrop, with more options in the integrations directory. Add one with 

eve add instrumentation/
, or use the instrumentation APIs to build your own integration.

Traces now show when an agent is waiting for a person, including tool approvals, questions, budget prompts, and sign-ins. They record model selections and approval decisions alongside model usage and cost, and follow calls into MCP servers and remote agents.

You choose what eve collects for tracing. Content you exclude from collection stays out of every destination. You can filter out spans or redact inputs and outputs per destination. Private conversations in production send only metadata by default, without prompts or tool results. The OpenTelemetry guide explains these controls.

On Vercel, Agent Runs uses the same traces to show sessions, model calls, tool execution, subagent activity, and approval decisions in the dashboard. When 

eve deploy
creates a new Vercel project, it sets up trace sampling automatically. See the Agent Runs guide for setup and configuration.

Copy link to headingLower agent turn latency

At the start of September, our hosted stress test on Vercel Workflows took a median of 3.036s per turn. In 1.0, the same 100-turn workload took 414ms. The test sends messages one at a time, with one immediate mock-model response and no tool calls per turn. We measure from sending a message until the turn finishes, capturing eve and Workflow overhead without the time a model takes to generate a response.

We worked with the Workflow team on spec 9, which gives each run a single orchestrator so background steps no longer replay the workflow. The team also moved event and stream writes to WebSockets and cut redundant history reads. eve agents get these improvements through Workflow SDK.

eve also caches the information it needs to route messages to each session and can move idle sessions to a newer deployment between turns. Web UIs can prewarm a session before the first message arrives, so the first reply starts sooner.

Copy link to headingLower workflow costs for long agent sessions

For a 50-turn Evo Docs session, the estimated Vercel Workflows cost drops from 5.4¢ to 1.3¢, about 76% lower. That assumes roughly two model steps per turn and 30-day retention. eve now uses Workflow SDK 5.5 and saves only the conversation data that changed between turns. We've also cut repeated work in workflow steps, checkpoints, and sandbox setup:

  • Workflow steps save changes and refer back to data already stored, instead of repeatedly copying a growing conversation into each step. Steps that don't need history no longer receive it.

  • Checkpoints store references to image files returned by tools, so they don't have to copy the image bytes each time.

  • Sandboxes from prepared snapshots skip repeated setup. Stop a sandbox and keep its files for reuse. Cleanup starts when the session ends.

The storage changes are part of the open-source Workflow SDK, so agents you host yourself on other Workflow backends also store less duplicate session data. The cost estimate above uses Vercel Workflows pricing.

On Vercel, workflow steps run on Fluid compute. They need extra storage writes for inputs above the payload size limit, so sending less session data helps keep turn times consistent as sessions grow. Images and files can still require those writes.

For model calls, tool and skill listings can stay out of the initial prompt until they're needed. Connection tools run through 

eve__search
and 
eve__tool
, so each search no longer has to expand the model's tool list. We also changed how eve marks parts of a prompt for provider caching, so more content can be reused between calls.

During an earlier migration to eve, an engineer at Evisions reported:

Transitioning to Eve delivered immediate, high impact results. To name a few, we were able to cut out 25k lines of code, cut our AI costs in half, and improved runtime by 66%.Chris Fleissner

Copy link to headingShare agent capabilities with extensions

Since the preview, we've added extensions so teams can share tools, skills, instructions, connections, channels, schedules, hooks, and subagents without copying files between agents. You can use extensions from the extensions directory or create your own with 

npx eve@latest extension init
.

For example, agent-browser adds browser automation, Mux Video adds tools for video assets and clips, and Link adds wallet and purchase tools.

eve builds workspace extensions from source and reloads changes during development. You can update shared capabilities in one package and try the changes in your agents as you work.

Copy link to headingBuild coding agents with eve’s shared tools

The 1.0 code extension builds on eve’s default file tools, adding coding instructions and skills that follow your repository’s 

AGENTS.md
. It's included in the 
eve
package, so there's nothing extra to install. Give it a repository in its sandbox and your agent can investigate code, edit files, and run the project's checks. It uses the same harness and extension system as your other agents, so you can replace or disable tools, override skills, and add your own instructions.

See the benchmark results for comparisons with other coding harnesses using the same tasks and model.

Add the coding extension to your agent:

      
eve add extension/code

Add the coding extension to an eve agent

The companion 

eve/extensions/git
adds GitHub and pull request workflows, using credentials and authorization you configure. On Vercel, the optional remote self-modification extension lets your agent propose changes to its own source in a draft pull request. You review the changes, merge them, and deploy.

Copy link to headingBuild with the same public APIs eve uses

We built eve's subagents, sleep, and question tools on the same workflow system you can use through 

defineWorkflowTool
. Your tools can return a result, start a background task, or keep accepting messages as a resumable task. They can wait for a person, webhook, or timer without keeping compute running, and their runs survive restarts. You don't need a separate background-job system to coordinate that work.

Once you've defined a 

reviewer
subagent, this tool returns a receipt immediately. The 
task
body waits for the reviewer's result, which is delivered to the model in a later message: 
      
import { defineWorkflowTool } from "eve/tools";import { z } from "zod";
export default defineWorkflowTool({  description: "Ask the reviewer to check these notes.",  inputSchema: z.object({ notes: z.string() }),  async task({ notes }, ctx) {    "use workflow";    const response = await ctx.agent("reviewer").send(notes, {      signal: ctx.abortSignal,    });    return await response.result();  },});

Delegate a review to a subagent

Been stress-testing crash recovery in @eve, and it's really solid: approvals and finished steps come back cleanly after a restart.George Shostakovych

Copy link to headingUpgrade to eve 1.0

If you already have an eve agent, the 1.0 upgrade guide walks through the changes to extension builds, agent APIs, session events, clients, and saved history. Follow it before deploying your upgrade.

eve follows semantic versioning, so breaking changes to stable APIs only happen in major releases. Experimental and internal APIs, including experimental fields, can change between major releases.

To work through the upgrade with your coding agent, copy this prompt:

Read https://eve.dev/docs/guides/upgrade and inspect this project's eve version and configuration. Upgrade it to eve 1.0, following the guide's order and the sections that apply. Update extensions, agent code, event consumers, clients, and saved history where needed. Run the project's typecheck, eve build, and relevant tests. Summarize the changes and any remaining manual migration or deployment steps.

Upgrade an existing project with your coding agent

Copy link to headingCreate your first eve agent

Start in the terminal to build locally, use the browser builder to create and deploy an agent, or choose a template for your use case.

Copy link to headingStart in the terminal

Create a new agent from the CLI with Node.js 24 or newer:

      
npx eve@latest init my-agent

Create a new eve agent

In an interactive terminal, this installs dependencies and opens the eve terminal UI. If your selected team has AI Gateway access, you can start chatting without creating a Vercel project or copying an API key. eve can use your existing Vercel CLI credentials to call models through AI Gateway locally. Use 

/login
to sign in to other connections.

In 

eve dev
, you can ask the agent to add a tool, change its instructions, or write a skill. With self-modification, it edits its own source and reloads the change for the next turn.

Copy link to headingStart in the browser

From the Vercel dashboard, the agent builder scaffolds an agent, creates its Git repo, and deploys it. Go to Add New → Agent, pick a model, and add web chat or Slack along the way.

Copy link to headingStart from a template

Choose an eve template for your use case:

Learn more in the eve docs.
